messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Spanish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Spanish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table (Spanish translation from Step 2)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|-------------------|--------| | Vedi | Imperative “see / behold” | Mira | “look / behold” | OK | | la | Definite article, fem. sg. | la | “the” (fem. sg.) | OK | | bestia | “the creature that is the causal factor” | bestia | “beast” | OK | | per | Preposition introducing cause | por | “by / because of” | OK | | cu' | Relative pronoun “which” (refers to *bestia*) | la cual | “which” (fem.) | OK | | io | 1st sg. personal pronoun, subject | *(omitted)* | “I” | UNNECESSARY | | mi | Reflexive pronoun, marks self‑directed action | me | “me” | OK | | volsi | Past historic “turned” | giré | “turned” | OK | | aiutami | Imperative “help me” | ayúdame | “help me” | OK | | da | Preposition “against” | contra | “against” | OK | | lei | 3rd sg. feminine pronoun, object of preposition | ella | “her” | OK | | famoso | Adjective “famous” | famoso | “famous” | OK | | saggio | Noun “sage” (vocative) | sabio | “sage” | OK | | ch'ella | Conjunction + pronoun “for she” | pues ella | “for she” | OK | | mi (2nd) | Pronoun, experiencer of trembling | me | “me” | OK | | fa | Causative verb “makes” | hace | “makes” | OK | | tremar | Infinitive “to tremble” | temblar | “to tremble” | OK | | le | Definite article, fem. pl. | las | “the” (fem. pl.) | OK | | vene | Noun “veins” | venas | “veins” | OK | | e | Coordinating conjunction “and” | y | “and” | OK | | i | Definite article, masc. pl. | los | “the” (masc. pl.) | OK | | polsi | Noun “pulses” | pulsos | “pulses” | OK |
### Items Requiring Attention - **io** – marked **UNNECESSARY** because Spanish normally omits the subject pronoun; the meaning is conveyed by the verb *giré*. No other tokens are missing, wrong, or grammatically mismatched.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Spanish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
